organizations.publicNote: German recording company active from 1925 to 1972; the linked discs use Electrola as their imprint. In 1972 Electrola-Gesellschaft and Carl Lindström GmbH were merged into the successor company EMI Electrola. The designation E.G. belongs to a record series, not to the organization’s name.

sources.fullCitation: Marek Weber und sein Orchester, refrain sung by Leo Moll. “Spiel’ mir auf der Balalaika einen russischen Tango.” Electrola E.G. 2392, matrix 00499-1; recorded in Berlin, 18 August 1931, released October 1931; also issued as His Master’s Voice AM 3741. Session and issue data from the Electrola label list at musiktiteldb.de, based on the Discographie der deutschen Tanzmusik. Digital transfer on YouTube, video Oq4sWv9khw4.
sources.title: Spiel’ mir auf der Balalaika einen russischen Tango — Electrola E.G. 2392
sources.creator: Marek Weber und sein Orchester; Leo Moll, vocal refrain
sources.researchNote: The transfer description dates the recording to 1932, whereas the Electrola label list gives a Berlin session on 18 August 1931 and an October 1931 release. The session-based chronology is preferred.

sources.shortCitation: YouTube, Marek Weber and Austin Egen, “Tränen weint jede Frau so gern”
sources.fullCitation: Marek Weber und sein Orchester, refrain sung by Austin Egen. “Tränen weint jede Frau so gern.” Tango. Digital transfer on YouTube; the upload identifies His Master’s Voice / Electrola and gives the year as 1929.
sources.title: Tränen weint jede Frau so gern — Marek Weber, YouTube
sources.creator: Marek Weber und sein Orchester, Refraingesang: Austin Egen
sources.researchNote: The upload identifies Marek Weber und sein Orchester with Austin Egen, a His Master’s Voice / Electrola issue and the year 1929, but supplies no catalogue or matrix number and does not show the disc label. It does not distinguish recording from issue year. Nico Dostal’s arrangement credit, Kaper’s music credit and Fritz Rotter’s words credit are uploader-supplied, not label transcriptions. The separate Tauber session documented for the same song does not identify this Weber transfer.

sources.shortCitation: Electrola E.G. 2271, “Du lieber Geiger, spiel’ einen Tango für mich” (Marek Weber, 1931)
sources.fullCitation: Marek Weber und sein Orchester. “Du lieber Geiger, spiel’ einen Tango für mich.” Electrola E.G. 2271, matrix OD267-1, recorded in Berlin on 24 March 1931 and released June 1931. Digital transfer published on YouTube by 78rpm Musik on 27 April 2025; discographic data from the Electrola label list at musiktiteldb.de.
sources.title: Du lieber Geiger, spiel’ einen Tango für mich — Electrola E.G. 2271
sources.creator: Marek Weber und sein Orchester
sources.researchNote: The Electrola label list, drawing on the Discographie der deutschen Tanzmusik, describes the side as instrumental. This conflicts with the transfer description, which calls it a dance-orchestra recording with refrain vocal. The label is not shown in the upload.

sources.fullCitation: Marek Weber und sein Orchester, refrain credited as Leo Moll. “Signorina aus Brioni.” Tango; label credits Fritz Rotter and Dr. Kaper for music and text. Electrola E.G. 2400, n.d. Shellac disc, Radiomuseum Hardthausen / Schallarchiv; filmed-label transfer on YouTube.
sources.title: Signorina aus Brioni — Electrola E.G. 2400
sources.creator: Marek Weber und sein Orchester, Refrain: Leo Moll
sources.researchNote: The uploader identifies the singer credited as Leo Moll as Leo Monosson and reports 1931 as the Electrola issue year. Neither that identification nor the issue year is printed on the filmed label; the year remains reported, without a newly established session date. The accompanying 1930 photograph depicts Brioni and does not date the disc. Discographic entries for other performers’ recordings of this song are not used to date Electrola E.G. 2400.

sources.shortCitation: YouTube, “Du bist in meinem Leben die erste Sensation” — uploader-identified recording
sources.fullCitation: Marek Weber und sein Orchester, vocal by John Hendrik. “Du bist in meinem Leben die erste Sensation.” Tango. Digital transfer on YouTube; the uploader identifies Electrola E.G. 2508 and gives the year as 1932.
sources.title: Du bist in meinem Leben die erste Sensation — external listening reference
sources.creator: Marek Weber und sein Orchester, Gesang: John Hendrik
sources.researchNote: An uploader-created opening card gives Electrola E.G. 2508, matrix E-OD 795 / I and a recording date of 17 February 1932. The disc label is not shown and the card contains no authorship credits. The Electrola label list at musiktiteldb.de instead lists E.G. 2508 against “Spanischer Zigeunertanz” (OD 773-1) and “Die alte Spieluhr” (OD770-1), not this title. These descriptions conflict; the upload has not been identified with a verified historical pressing. Its year and performer details remain uploader-supplied, and it is retained as a listening reference rather than a verified description of E.G. 2508.

additionalLinks.label: Electrola label list — conflicting catalogue-number evidence

sources.fullCitation: Marek Weber und sein Orchester, dance orchestra with refrain vocal. “Margarete, wander mit mir ….” Fox-trot; label credits music and text to Fritz Rotter and Dr. B. Kaper. Electrola E.G. 2406, matrix 60-1740, n.d. Shellac disc, Radiomuseum Hardthausen / Schallarchiv; filmed-label transfer on YouTube.
sources.title: Margarete, wander mit mir … — Electrola E.G. 2406
sources.creator: Marek Weber und sein Orchester, Tanz-Orchester mit Refraingesang
sources.researchNote: The filmed label identifies Marek Weber und sein Orchester, Electrola E.G. 2406 and matrix 60-1740. R. Pfau’s Lexikon der deutschen Tanzmusik, part 6, printed p. 736, independently lists “EG 2406 Marek Weber” under “Margarethe wander mit mir”. Its general year 1931 is not a separately documented session or issue date. The source retains 1931 as the uploader-reported recording year. The uploader’s link to an Italian version does not identify or date this pressing.

additionalLinks.label: R. Pfau, Lexikon der deutschen Tanzmusik, part 6, p. 736

sources.fullCitation: Jack Hylton und sein Orchester, refrain sung by Siegfried Arno. “Das verliebte Orchester.” Fox-trot; label credits text and music to Fritz Rotter and Dr. B. Kaper. Electrola E.G. 2259, matrix 60-1496; recorded 11 March 1931, issue date not established. Shellac disc, Radiomuseum Hardthausen / Schallarchiv; filmed-label transfer on YouTube.
sources.title: Das verliebte Orchester — Electrola E.G. 2259
sources.creator: Jack Hylton und sein Orchester, Refrain: Siegfried Arno
sources.researchNote: The Jack Hylton website’s MP3 Downloads discography lists this title, Electrola EG-2259 and Siegfried Arno, with 11/03/31 in the “Recording Date” column. The structured date therefore identifies the session on 11 March 1931, not the commercial issue date. The label supplies the matrix and printed credits; the independent listing does not specify a take. The uploader’s general statement that Electrola issued the disc in 1931 remains distinct from this session evidence.

additionalLinks.label: Jack Hylton — MP3 Downloads discography, “Das Verliebte Orchester”

sources.shortCitation: His Master’s Voice E.G. 2481, “’S wird schon wieder besser” (Dolly Haas, 1932)
sources.fullCitation: Dolly Haas with a chamber orchestra directed by Hans Sommer. “’S wird schon wieder besser.” YouTube transfer published by Marconiphone; the upload identifies His Master’s Voice E.G. 2481, matrix 60-1853, credits the music to Jurmann and Kaper, associates the song with Liebe mit Bewährungsfrist and dates the recording to Berlin, 1932.
sources.title: ’S wird schon wieder besser — His Master’s Voice E.G. 2481
sources.creator: Dolly Haas; Kammerorchester, Hans Sommer, director
sources.researchNote: The catalogue and matrix numbers, performers, film association, music credits and recording year are supplied by the upload description; the disc label is not shown. No independent label or session record has been matched to this transfer. The source retains the uploader’s specific disc identification as reported, not verified, and 1932 is not treated as an established issue date.

sources.shortCitation: Electrola EG 2135, “Ach, Otto, Otto…!” (Marek Weber with Siegfried Arno, 1931)
sources.fullCitation: Marek Weber und sein Orchester, refrain sung by Siegfried Arno. “Ach, Otto, Otto…!” Foxtrot; Electrola EG 2135, matrix BD 9264-2, playing time 3:12; recorded in the Beethoven-Saal, Berlin, and released in January 1931; also issued as His Master’s Voice AM 3450. Music by Bronisław Kaper, words by Fritz Rotter. Entry in the Electrola label list and the title list at musiktiteldb.de, both following the Discographie der deutschen Kleinkunst, vol. 1.
sources.title: Ach, Otto, Otto…! — Electrola EG 2135
sources.creator: Marek Weber und sein Orchester; Siegfried Arno, refrain vocal

sources.shortCitation: Electrola EG 2228, “Ich steh’ im Schnee und wart’ auf Dich” (Mitja Nikisch with Paul Dorn, 1931)
sources.fullCitation: Mitja Nikisch und sein Orchester, refrain sung by Paul Dorn. “Ich steh’ im Schnee und wart’ auf Dich.” Foxtrot from Die grosse Attraktion. Electrola E.G. 2228, matrix OD106-2, recorded Berlin, 15 March 1931; also issued as His Master’s Voice AM 3411 and HMV R 14602. Electrola label and title lists at musiktiteldb.de, following the Discographie der deutschen Tanzmusik, vol. 4.
sources.title: Ich steh’ im Schnee und wart’ auf Dich — Electrola EG 2228
sources.creator: Mitja Nikisch und sein Orchester; Paul Dorn, refrain vocal
sources.researchNote: The discographic entry assigns both words and music to Bronisław Kaper. Hofmeister (February 1931, p. 35) registers the song under Kaper with words by Fritz Rotter and Armin Robinson; the discographic lyric credit is not used to replace that. The Electrola label list gives 15 March 1931 in its recording-date column and leaves the release-date column empty. HMV R 14602 is a parallel record issue, not a U.S. copyright renewal identifier.

sources.shortCitation: Electrola E.G. 2532, “Ganz ohne Liebe wär’ das Leben so bescheiden”
sources.fullCitation: Marek Weber und sein Orchester. “Ganz ohne Liebe wär’ das Leben so bescheiden.” Fox-trot with refrain vocal; music by Walter Jurmann and Bronislaw Kaper, words by Fritz Rotter. Electrola E.G. 2532. YouTube transfer by Underlabelcrack; the uploader reports matrix OD 879-2 and a Berlin recording session around March 1932.
sources.title: Ganz ohne Liebe wär’ das Leben so bescheiden — Electrola E.G. 2532
sources.creator: Marek Weber und sein Orchester
sources.researchNote: R. Pfau’s Lexikon der deutschen Tanzmusik, part 3, printed p. 321, independently lists this title, its Kaper–Jurmann/Rotter credit, the film Skandal in der Parkstraße and “EG 2532 Marek Weber”. Its general year 1932 is not a separately documented issue or session date. The approximate March 1932 Berlin session and matrix OD 879-2 remain uploader-supplied. The uploader tentatively names the refrain singer as “John Hendrick”; this is not treated as a confirmed singer identification. The particular transferred pressing and take remain unverified.

additionalLinks.label: R. Pfau, Lexikon der deutschen Tanzmusik, part 3, p. 321
